title: mRNA Technology: Beyond COVID-19 Vaccines
description: Expanding the mRNA platform to personalised cancer vaccines, rare disease treatments, and infectious disease prevention. Covers LNP optimisation, self-amplifying mRNA, and ongoing Phase II/III trials.
speaker: Dr. Katalin Karikó

title: Engineering Metabolic Pathways for Bioproduction
description: Using synthetic biology to engineer microbes and yeast for producing biofuels, pharmaceuticals, and specialty chemicals. Covers flux balance analysis, pathway optimisation, and industrial fermentation scale-up.
speaker: Prof. Jay Keasling

title: AI-Driven Protein Engineering and De Novo Design
description: Using deep learning to engineer proteins with novel functions — ProteinMPNN and RFdiffusion for de novo design, directed evolution with ML-guided fitness landscapes, and therapeutic enzyme engineering.
speaker: Dr. David Baker

title: Organoids and 3D Cell Culture for Drug Testing
description: Patient-derived organoids as predictive models for drug response. Applications in oncology, GI disease, and rare genetic disorders. Integration with high-content imaging and AI-based phenotypic analysis.
speaker: Prof. Hans Clevers

title: Antibody Engineering: Bispecifics, Nanobodies, and ADCs
description: Next-generation antibody formats including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, and camelid nanobodies. Engineering strategies for improved specificity, half-life extension, and reduced immunogenicity.
speaker: Dr. Paul Carter

title: Biotech Regulatory Landscape: FDA and EMA in 2026
description: Navigating regulatory pathways for biologics, ATMPs, and AI-assisted drug development. FDA CDER digital health guidance, EMA adaptive licensing, real-world evidence requirements, and post-approval commitments.
speaker: Dr. Rachel Sherman

title: CAR-T Therapy: From Hematology to Solid Tumors
description: Progress in chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy beyond blood cancers. Engineering armoured CAR-Ts to survive the immunosuppressive solid tumor microenvironment, next-generation CAR designs, and in-vivo manufacturing.
speaker: Dr. Carl June

title: AAV Vector Design for In-Vivo Gene Delivery
description: Adeno-associated virus capsid engineering for tissue-specific tropism, immune evasion, and high-capacity payloads. Covers directed evolution of capsids, manufacturing challenges, and clinical results in neuromuscular disease.
speaker: Dr. James Wilson

title: Base Editing and Prime Editing: Precision Beyond CRISPR
description: Chemical and mechanistic basis of base editors (CBEs, ABEs) and prime editing. Clinical applications for correcting point mutations in genetic diseases, safety profiles, and comparison with HDR-based approaches.
speaker: Prof. David Liu

title: Lentiviral Vectors in Clinical Gene Therapy
description: Lentiviral vector design for stable genomic integration in HSCs and T cells. Clinical outcomes in ADA-SCID, X-linked CGD, and metachromatic leukodystrophy. Genotoxicity monitoring and insertional oncogenesis risk.
speaker: Dr. Luigi Naldini

title: Gene Therapy Manufacturing: From Bench to Commercial Scale
description: Overcoming biomanufacturing bottlenecks for viral vector and cell therapy products. Automation, closed-system bioprocessing, QC analytics, cost-of-goods reduction strategies, and CDMO partnerships.
speaker: Dr. Katherine High

title: iPSC-Derived Cell Therapies: Allogeneic off-the-Shelf Products
description: Generating therapeutic cell types (NK cells, T cells, cardiomyocytes) from induced pluripotent stem cells. HLA engineering for immune evasion, scalable differentiation protocols, and clinical trial status.
speaker: Prof. Shinya Yamanaka

title: In-Vivo CRISPR Delivery: LNPs, Exosomes, and Beyond
description: Non-viral delivery of CRISPR-Cas components for in-vivo gene editing. Lipid nanoparticle formulation, extracellular vesicle engineering, and emerging delivery modalities for liver, lung, and CNS targets.
speaker: Prof. Daniel Anderson

title: Designing Genetic Circuits with Boolean Logic
description: Engineering programmable gene circuits that implement logic gates, memory elements, and analog computation in living cells. Applications in biosensing, therapeutic delivery, and biomanufacturing process control.
speaker: Prof. Jim Collins

title: Cell-Free Synthetic Biology and Point-of-Care Diagnostics
description: Freeze-dried cell-free expression systems for portable diagnostics. SHERLOCK and DETECTR platforms, toehold switch biosensors, and field-deployable tests for infectious disease and environmental monitoring.
speaker: Dr. Michael Jewett

title: Directed Evolution: Engineering Enzymes with Machine Learning
description: Combining laboratory evolution with ML models to navigate fitness landscapes efficiently. Protein language models for variant scoring, active learning for experimental design, and industrial enzyme engineering case studies.
speaker: Dr. Frances Arnold

title: Minimal Cells and Synthetic Genomes
description: JCVI-syn3A and the quest for a minimal viable genome. Whole-genome synthesis, genome recoding for expanded genetic codes, and what minimal cells teach us about the essential functions of life.
speaker: Dr. Clyde Hutchison

title: Biosafety, Biosecurity, and Ethics in Synthetic Biology
description: Governance frameworks for dual-use research of concern in synthetic biology. DNA synthesis screening, gain-of-function debate, iGEM safety policies, and international biosecurity norms in an era of AI-assisted design.
speaker: Dr. Kenneth Oye

title: Living Therapeutics: Engineered Bacteria for Medicine
description: Programming gut bacteria to sense disease biomarkers and deliver therapeutics in-situ. Engineered E. coli and Lactobacillus for IBD, metabolic disease, and cancer immunotherapy. Containment strategies and clinical trial results.
speaker: Prof. Timothy Lu

title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing: Analysis Pipelines at Scale
description: End-to-end scRNA-seq analysis with Scanpy, Seurat, and scVI. Cell type annotation, trajectory inference with PAGA and Monocle, batch correction methods, and handling datasets of 10 million+ cells from atlas projects.
speaker: Prof. Fabian Theis

title: AlphaFold 3 and the Future of Structural Biology
description: AlphaFold 3 extended capabilities — predicting protein-DNA, protein-RNA, and protein-small molecule complexes. Impact on structural genomics, target identification in drug discovery, and the limits of current structure prediction.
speaker: Dr. John Jumper

title: Multi-Omics Integration with Deep Learning
description: Fusing genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics for comprehensive disease modelling. Covers MOFA+, multi-modal VAEs, and graph-based integration methods for patient stratification and biomarker discovery.
speaker: Prof. Nir Yosef

title: Metagenomics and the Human Microbiome
description: Analysing microbial communities from shotgun sequencing data. Assembly, binning, taxonomic classification with Kraken2 and MetaPhlAn, functional annotation with HUMAnN, and linking microbiome composition to host disease phenotypes.
speaker: Prof. Curtis Huttenhower

title: Genome-Wide Association Studies at Biobank Scale
description: Running GWAS on 500k+ individuals from UK Biobank and All of Us. Controlling for population stratification, fine-mapping causal variants with SuSiE and FINEMAP, and translating GWAS hits into biological mechanisms.
speaker: Prof. Mark Daly

title: Spatial Transcriptomics: Mapping Gene Expression in Tissue
description: Technologies for spatially resolved gene expression — 10x Visium, Slide-seq, MERFISH, and Xenium. Computational methods for spatial clustering, ligand-receptor cell communication, and 3D tissue atlas reconstruction.
speaker: Dr. Rahul Satija

title: Drug Repurposing with Biological Knowledge Graphs
description: Mining biomedical knowledge graphs (Hetionet, SPOKE, Open Targets) for drug repurposing candidates. Graph neural network link prediction, embedding methods, and validation against real-world clinical trial outcomes.
speaker: Prof. Marinka Zitnik

title: Long-Read Genome Assembly: Algorithms and Applications
description: De novo genome assembly from PacBio HiFi and Oxford Nanopore reads. HiFiasm, Verkko, and hifiasm-meta algorithms, T2T chromosome-level assemblies, and the complete human pangenome reference project.
speaker: Dr. Heng Li

title: RNA Structure Prediction with Deep Learning
description: Predicting secondary and tertiary RNA structure using transformer-based models. EternaFold, RoseTTAFoldNA, and RhoFold+. Applications in mRNA vaccine design, ribozyme engineering, and RNA-targeting drug discovery.
speaker: Dr. Rhiju Das

title: Comparative Genomics and Phylogenomics
description: Reconstructing evolutionary history from thousands of genomes. Scalable phylogenetic methods (ASTRAL, IQ-TREE), whole-genome alignment, synteny analysis, and detecting positive selection in protein-coding genes.
speaker: Prof. Tandy Warnow

title: Epigenomics: Chromatin Accessibility and 3D Genome Organisation
description: ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN, and Hi-C analysis for mapping regulatory landscapes. Identifying enhancer-promoter interactions, TAD boundaries, and epigenetic changes in cancer and development.
speaker: Prof. William Noble

title: Single-Cell Multi-Omics: CITE-seq, ATAC-seq, and Spatial
description: Simultaneous profiling of gene expression, chromatin accessibility, and protein levels at single-cell resolution. Computational frameworks for multimodal data integration and regulatory network inference.
speaker: Dr. Aviv Regev

title: Protein Language Models for Function Prediction
description: ESM-2, ESM-3, ProtTrans, and Ankh as universal protein encoders. Zero-shot variant effect prediction, remote homology detection, and learning evolutionary constraints from sequence alone.
speaker: Dr. Alexander Rives

title: Pangenome Graphs: Beyond the Linear Reference Genome
description: The human pangenome reference consortium and graph-based genome representations. minigraph-cactus construction, genotyping structural variants with vg, and implications for population genomics and rare disease diagnosis.
speaker: Prof. Benedict Paten

title: Deep Learning for Variant Calling: DeepVariant and Beyond
description: Pileup image-based variant calling with DeepVariant, PEPPER-Margin-DeepVariant for long reads, and recent models using transformer architectures. Benchmarking on GIAB and clinical sequencing datasets.
speaker: Dr. Andrew Carroll

title: Gene Regulatory Networks from Single-Cell Data
description: Inferring transcription factor regulons and gene regulatory networks from scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq. SCENIC+, GRNBoost2, and causal approaches to distinguish drivers from downstream targets in development and disease.
speaker: Dr. Cole Trapnell

title: Functional Annotation of Non-Coding Variants
description: Predicting the functional impact of variants in regulatory regions using Enformer, Borzoi, and sequence-to-function models. Prioritising non-coding GWAS hits and identifying causal regulatory variants in complex disease.
speaker: Dr. Manolis Kellis

title: Nanopore Direct RNA Sequencing and Epitranscriptomics
description: Direct sequencing of RNA molecules with nanopore technology — full-length isoform detection, m6A and pseudouridine modification calling, and real-time transcriptome monitoring without reverse transcription.
speaker: Dr. Jared Simpson

title: Clinical Genomics: Rare Disease Diagnosis at Scale
description: Whole-genome sequencing in clinical diagnostics. Automated variant prioritisation with AI, phenotype-driven analysis with HPO terms, short-read vs long-read for structural variant detection, and reporting standards.
speaker: Dr. Zornitza Stark

title: Superconducting Qubits: Milestones and the Road to Fault Tolerance
description: Progress report on superconducting qubit systems from IBM, Google, and Amazon. Current gate fidelities, qubit counts, and coherence times. What separates today's NISQ processors from fault-tolerant quantum computing.
speaker: Prof. John Martinis

title: Quantum Error Correction: Surface Codes in Practice
description: How surface codes protect logical qubits from physical errors. Threshold theorems, minimum-weight perfect matching decoders, neural network decoders, and what it takes to achieve fault-tolerant logical operations.
speaker: Prof. Barbara Terhal

title: Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers: IonQ and Quantinuum
description: The physics and engineering of trapped-ion systems. All-to-all connectivity, high two-qubit gate fidelities, and the QCCD architecture for scaling. Benchmarking against superconducting systems on practical workloads.
speaker: Prof. Christopher Monroe

title: Topological Qubits and Non-Abelian Anyons
description: The physics of Majorana zero modes as a basis for topologically protected qubits. Microsoft's recent experimental evidence, the challenge of braiding operations, and the long-term promise of hardware-level error protection.
speaker: Dr. Sankar Das Sarma

title: Quantum Networking and the Quantum Internet
description: Building quantum networks for secure communication, distributed quantum computing, and clock synchronisation. Quantum repeaters, entanglement distribution over optical fibre, and the architecture of a future quantum internet.
speaker: Prof. Stephanie Wehner

title: Quantum Advantage: Real Applications vs Hype
description: Critical assessment of claimed quantum speedups. Variational quantum eigensolvers for chemistry, quantum optimisation with QAOA, quantum ML, and an honest analysis of where practical quantum advantage is achievable today.
speaker: Dr. Scott Aaronson

title: Gravitational Wave Astronomy: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA O4 Results
description: Key discoveries from the fourth observing run: binary black hole and neutron star mergers, tests of general relativity with compact binaries, Hubble constant measurements from gravitational wave sirens, and multi-messenger observations.
speaker: Prof. Gabriela González

title: Particle Physics: LHC Run 3 and Future Colliders
description: Latest results from ATLAS and CMS at 13.6 TeV — precision Higgs measurements, searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model, and the physics case for FCC-ee, ILC, and a muon collider.
speaker: Prof. Fabiola Gianotti

title: Dark Matter: Direct and Indirect Detection Experiments
description: Status of dark matter searches at LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX for WIMPs; Fermi-LAT and CTA for indirect annihilation signals; and axion experiments (ADMX, ABRACADABRA). Where do we stand on dark matter detection in 2026?
speaker: Prof. Priscilla Cushman

title: JWST and the Early Universe: Cosmology Surprises
description: JWST discoveries reshaping our understanding of the early universe — unexpectedly massive early galaxies, reionisation epoch measurements, and tensions with the standard ΛCDM cosmological model. What does it all mean?
speaker: Dr. Jane Rigby

title: Machine Learning in High-Energy Physics
description: Deep learning for jet tagging, particle reconstruction, and event classification at the LHC. Graph neural networks for tracking, anomaly detection for model-agnostic new physics searches, and fast ML inference at the trigger level.
speaker: Prof. Kyle Cranmer

title: Nuclear Fusion Energy: Progress at ITER and Private Ventures
description: Status of ITER construction and first plasma timeline. Record-breaking results from NIF's inertial confinement and Commonwealth Fusion's SPARC high-temperature superconducting magnet. The race to commercial fusion power.
speaker: Dr. Kim Budil

title: Black Hole Imaging: Event Horizon Telescope Science
description: Results from EHT observations of M87* and Sgr A*. Black hole shadow morphology, jet launching physics, and upcoming ngEHT improvements for real-time black hole movies and polarimetric imaging.
speaker: Dr. Sheperd Doeleman

title: Exoplanet Atmospheres with JWST Spectroscopy
description: JWST transmission and emission spectroscopy of exoplanet atmospheres — detecting CO2, methane, water, and searching for biosignature gases. Rocky planet characterisation and prospects for habitability assessment.
speaker: Dr. Nikku Madhusudhan

title: Fast Radio Bursts: Origins and Cosmological Applications
description: The growing FRB sample from CHIME and ASKAP — localising sources, identifying repeaters, host galaxy properties, and using FRBs as cosmological probes to measure baryon density and intergalactic magnetic fields.
speaker: Dr. Victoria Kaspi

title: Multimessenger Astronomy: Neutrinos, Photons, and Gravitational Waves
description: IceCube astrophysical neutrino sources, coordinated follow-up with Fermi-LAT and Cherenkov telescopes, and the promise of combined GW+EM observations for understanding extreme astrophysical events.
speaker: Prof. Francis Halzen

title: Machine Learning for Large Astronomical Surveys
description: AI methods for the Vera Rubin Observatory LSST, Euclid, and SKA surveys. Automated transient classification, photometric redshift estimation, weak gravitational lensing analysis, and anomaly detection for rare astrophysical phenomena.
speaker: Prof. Alex Szalay

title: The Roman Space Telescope and Next-Generation Observatories
description: Science goals of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope — dark energy wide-field survey, microlensing exoplanet census, and coronagraphic direct imaging. Looking ahead to Habitable Worlds Observatory.
speaker: Dr. Natalie Batalha

title: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials: MACE, NequIP, and CHGNet
description: Replacing expensive DFT with equivariant neural network potentials for large-scale molecular dynamics. Accuracy benchmarks on reaction barriers, phonons, and phase transitions. Active learning for dataset construction.
speaker: Prof. Michele Ceriotti

title: Quantum Chemistry with Machine Learning: Solving the Schrödinger Equation
description: Neural network wavefunctions (FermiNet, PauliNet, DeepErwin) for solving the electronic structure problem. Scaling to larger molecules, excited states, and the prospect of accuracy beyond coupled cluster methods.
speaker: Prof. Frank Noé

title: Free Energy Calculations for Protein-Ligand Binding
description: Alchemical free energy perturbation, thermodynamic integration, and enhanced sampling methods for predicting binding affinities. Prospective accuracy benchmarks, automation platforms, and integration into drug discovery pipelines.
speaker: Dr. John Chodera

title: Molecular Dynamics at Millisecond Timescales
description: Accessing biologically relevant timescales with specialised hardware (Anton 3), adaptive sampling (metadynamics, REST2), and Markov state models. Applications in protein folding, conformational change, and drug binding kinetics.
speaker: Prof. David Shaw

title: Automated Reaction Mechanism Discovery
description: Computational tools for exploring chemical reaction networks without human bias — RDKit, autodE, ORCA-based workflows, and ML-guided transition state search. Applications in catalysis, photochemistry, and combustion.
speaker: Prof. Markus Reiher

title: Computational Catalyst Design with Machine Learning
description: Accelerating heterogeneous catalyst discovery using DFT-ML hybrid workflows, the Open Catalyst 2020/2022 datasets, and graph neural network adsorption energy predictors. Active learning cycles and experimental validation.
speaker: Dr. Zachary Ulissi

title: Generative Models for Drug-Like Molecule Design
description: Designing novel drug candidates with generative AI — graph VAEs, diffusion models (DiffSBDD, TargetDiff), flow matching, and reinforcement learning for multi-objective molecular optimisation guided by docking scores and synthesisability.
speaker: Prof. Alán Aspuru-Guzik

title: Retrosynthesis Planning with Transformer Models
description: Treating chemistry as a language — SMILES-based transformers for single-step reaction prediction and multi-step retrosynthetic planning. AiZynthFinder, ASKCOS, and Chemist benchmarks for evaluating planning quality.
speaker: Dr. Philippe Schwaller

title: ADMET Prediction with Graph Neural Networks
description: Predicting absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity from molecular structure. TDC benchmark performance, uncertainty quantification for safety-critical predictions, and handling data imbalance in toxicity datasets.
speaker: Dr. Bharath Ramsundar

title: Materials Discovery for Next-Generation Battery Technology
description: Applying GNNs to predict crystal stability, ionic conductivity, and electrochemical stability windows for solid electrolytes and cathode materials. The Materials Project and high-throughput DFT screening workflows.
speaker: Prof. Kristin Persson

title: Green Chemistry and AI-Assisted Sustainable Synthesis
description: Using machine learning to design greener synthetic routes — predicting reaction conditions, minimising E-factor waste, replacing hazardous reagents, and incorporating atom economy metrics into automated retrosynthesis planning.
speaker: Prof. Klavs Jensen

title: Self-Driving Laboratories for Accelerated Chemical Discovery
description: Autonomous experimental platforms that close the loop between prediction and synthesis. Robotic liquid handlers, in-line analytical chemistry (HPLC, NMR), Bayesian optimisation strategies, and case studies in reaction condition optimisation.
speaker: Prof. Jason Hein

title: Fragment-Based Drug Discovery Enhanced by AI
description: Combining fragment screening with ML-guided elaboration for hit-to-lead optimisation. Structure-activity relationship modelling, generative fragment growing, and integration with cryo-EM for rapid hit confirmation.
speaker: Dr. Chris Murray

title: Covalent Drugs: Targeting Undruggable Proteins
description: Rational design of covalent inhibitors for historically intractable targets — KRAS G12C, EGFR, and BTK. Warhead selection, selectivity profiling with activity-based proteomics, and clinical success stories.
speaker: Prof. Kevan Shokat

title: PROTACs and Targeted Protein Degradation
description: Bifunctional molecules that recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to degrade disease-causing proteins. PROTAC design rules, hook effect, ternary complex modelling with ML, and clinical progress in oncology.
speaker: Prof. Craig Crews

title: Macrocycles as Therapeutics: Design and Permeability
description: Macrocyclic drug design for challenging targets like protein-protein interactions. Computational conformational sampling, passive permeability prediction, and ML-guided macrocycle library design.
speaker: Dr. Gisbert Schneider

title: Phenotypic Drug Discovery in the Age of AI
description: Revisiting phenotypic screening with modern tools: cell painting with morphological profiling, high-content imaging AI, and target deconvolution strategies using chemoproteomics and ML.
speaker: Prof. Stuart Schreiber

title: AI-Assisted Clinical Candidate Selection and Optimisation
description: Using predictive models to guide lead optimisation decisions — balancing potency, selectivity, ADMET, and synthesisability simultaneously. Multi-parameter optimisation platforms and human-AI collaborative workflows in pharma.
speaker: Dr. Anthony Bradley

title: State Space Models: Mamba and Hybrid Architectures
description: The rise of selective state space models as transformer alternatives for long sequences. S4, Mamba, and Mamba-2 mechanics, hybrid SSM-attention architectures, and benchmarks on language, audio, genomics, and video tasks.
speaker: Prof. Albert Gu

title: Vision Transformers in 2026: Efficiency, Scale, and Adaptation
description: State of vision transformers — DINOv2, SAM 2, and efficient architectures (EfficientViT). ViTs as universal visual encoders for downstream tasks, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and comparison with modern ConvNets.
speaker: Dr. Kaiming He

title: Neural Scaling Laws: Insights from Frontier Training
description: Empirical and theoretical analysis of how loss scales with compute, data, and parameters beyond Chinchilla. Data quality vs quantity, multimodal scaling, and what the loss curves predict about capabilities at 10^27 FLOPs.
speaker: Dr. Jared Kaplan

title: Efficient Inference: Quantisation, Pruning, and Speculative Decoding
description: Making large models fast and cheap to serve. INT4 quantisation with GPTQ and AWQ, structured pruning, knowledge distillation, and speculative decoding for 3–5× inference speedups without quality loss.
speaker: Dr. Song Han

title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Scientific Computing
description: Training neural networks that satisfy physical laws — PDEs, conservation equations, and symmetry constraints. Applications in fluid dynamics, heat transfer, and materials science. Comparison with traditional numerical solvers.
speaker: Prof. George Karniadakis

title: Geometric Deep Learning: Equivariance and Symmetry
description: Building neural networks that respect symmetries of the data — E(3) equivariance for molecular systems, gauge equivariance for lattice field theories, and the unifying framework of group theory in deep learning.
speaker: Prof. Max Welling

title: Deep Learning for Climate and Earth System Modelling
description: Neural weather prediction (GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, FourCastNet) vs traditional NWP. Downscaling climate projections, extreme event prediction, and emulating expensive physics-based Earth system models with diffusion models.
speaker: Dr. Stephan Rasp

title: Diffusion Models: Theory, Architectures, and New Frontiers
description: From DDPM to consistency models and flow matching — the unifying theory behind score-based generative models. DiT architectures, video diffusion (Sora), 3D generation, and scientific applications in drug design and materials.
speaker: Dr. Yang Song

title: Test-Time Compute and Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
description: Scaling inference compute for better reasoning — chain-of-thought prompting, self-consistency, tree-of-thought search, and the o1/o3 paradigm of thinking tokens. How much can we gain by thinking longer?
speaker: Dr. Noam Brown

title: Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Coordination and Reliability
description: Designing multi-agent systems where specialised LLMs collaborate on complex tasks. Orchestration frameworks, memory sharing, tool use, failure modes in agent pipelines, and evaluation methodologies for agentic behaviour.
speaker: Prof. Stuart Russell

title: World Models and Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
description: Learning compressed world models for planning and imagination. DREAMER, IRIS, and latent diffusion-based world models. Applications in robotics, game-playing, and autonomous driving without real-world rollouts.
speaker: Dr. David Ha

title: Hallucination Mitigation in Large Language Models
description: Understanding why LLMs confabulate and how to reduce it. Retrieval augmentation, chain-of-verification, calibration through RLHF, factuality fine-tuning, and benchmarks for measuring truthfulness in deployed systems.
speaker: Prof. Percy Liang

title: Neural Architecture Search and Automated ML in 2026
description: Where NAS stands today — differentiable architecture search, hardware-aware NAS, and one-shot supernets. LLMs as optimisers for architecture search, meta-learning for fast adaptation, and automated pipeline design.
speaker: Prof. Quoc Le

title: Spiking Neural Networks and Neuromorphic Computing
description: Biologically plausible learning with spike-timing-dependent plasticity, surrogate gradient training, and large-scale neuromorphic hardware (Intel Loihi 2, BrainScaleS-2). Energy efficiency benchmarks vs traditional ANNs.
speaker: Prof. Wolfgang Maass

title: Brain-Computer Interfaces: High-Bandwidth Neural Decoding
description: State of BCI technology — Utah arrays, Neuropixels, and high-density ECoG for motor and speech decoding. Neuralink clinical trial results, wireless implants, and deep learning decoders for real-time neural prosthetics.
speaker: Dr. Frank Guenther

title: Neural Population Dynamics and Dimensionality Reduction
description: Low-dimensional manifolds in high-dimensional neural recordings. GPFA, CEBRA, LFADS, and Poisson VAEs for extracting latent dynamics. What population-level analysis reveals about computation in cortex, cerebellum, and hippocampus.
speaker: Prof. Surya Ganguli

title: Connectomics: Mapping Complete Neural Wiring Diagrams
description: Electron microscopy reconstruction of complete nervous systems — the Drosophila hemibrain and C. elegans connectome. Automated proofreading with AI, synapse detection, and what wiring diagrams tell us about circuit function.
speaker: Dr. H. Sebastian Seung

title: Deep Learning as a Model of Visual Cortex
description: Comparing deep neural network representations to primate V1, V2, V4, and IT cortex. Predicting neural responses to natural images, texture synthesis as a model of V2, and the limits of current DNN brain models.
speaker: Prof. Nikolaus Kriegeskorte

title: Reinforcement Learning and Dopaminergic Reward Circuits
description: Parallels between temporal difference learning and dopamine neuron firing. Distributional RL as a model of the basal ganglia, successor representation in hippocampus, and computational psychiatry for modelling addiction and depression.
speaker: Prof. Matthew Botvinick

title: Neural Basis of Memory Consolidation: From Synapses to Systems
description: How memories are stabilised from short-term to long-term storage. Hippocampal-neocortical dialogue during sleep, sharp-wave ripples, systems consolidation theory, and evidence from engram cell studies in rodents and humans.
speaker: Prof. Susumu Tonegawa

title: Optogenetics at 15: Controlling Neural Circuits with Light
description: A retrospective on 15 years of optogenetics — channelrhodopsin variants, soma-targeted opsin expression, fibre photometry, and all-optical interrogation combining stimulation with calcium imaging for circuit dissection.
speaker: Prof. Karl Deisseroth

title: AI for Drug Discovery in Neurological Disorders
description: Machine learning approaches targeting Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, ALS, and psychiatric disorders. Microglial biology and neuroinflammation as drug targets, biomarker discovery from neuroimaging, and repurposing strategies.
speaker: Dr. Beth Stevens

title: Large-Scale Neural Recording: Neuropixels 3.0 and Beyond
description: Recording from thousands of neurons simultaneously with next-generation silicon probes. Spike sorting at scale (Kilosort4, MountainSort5), drift correction, multi-region recordings, and challenges for analysing terabyte-scale datasets.
speaker: Dr. Timothy Harris

title: Organoid Intelligence and Brain-on-Chip Systems
description: Cerebral organoids and assembloids as models of human brain development and disease. MEA recording from organoids, organoid-computer interfaces, learning in biological neural networks, and ethical considerations.
speaker: Prof. Thomas Hartung

title: Spatial Transcriptomics of the Brain: Allen Brain Cell Atlas
description: Mapping the complete cellular diversity of the mammalian brain with spatial transcriptomics. The Allen Brain Cell Atlas project, cell type taxonomy across brain regions, and integrating morphology, connectivity, and gene expression.
speaker: Dr. Hongkui Zeng

title: High-Entropy Alloys: Discovery and Design with Machine Learning
description: Using ML and high-throughput DFT to explore the vast compositional space of multi-principal element alloys. Property prediction for hardness, oxidation resistance, and irradiation tolerance with Gaussian process and neural network models.
speaker: Prof. Surya Kalidindi

title: Perovskite Solar Cells: Efficiency Records and Stability
description: Breaking 26% efficiency with perovskite single-junction and tandem cells. Understanding degradation mechanisms, encapsulation strategies, lead-free alternatives, and the path to IEC-certified 20-year outdoor stability.
speaker: Prof. Henry Snaith

title: 2D Materials Beyond Graphene: MoS₂, hBN, and Heterostructures
description: Physics and applications of transition metal dichalcogenides, hexagonal boron nitride, and van der Waals heterostructures. Moiré superlattices, unconventional superconductivity, valleytronics, and atomically thin optoelectronics.
speaker: Prof. Pablo Jarillo-Herrero

title: Solid-State Batteries: Electrolytes and Interfaces
description: Materials challenges for solid-state lithium batteries — oxide, sulfide, and polymer electrolytes. Interfacial resistance, lithium dendrite suppression, and ML-guided discovery of new solid electrolyte compositions for EV applications.
speaker: Prof. Yet-Ming Chiang

title: Metamaterials and Programmable Photonic Structures
description: Designing materials with electromagnetic properties not found in nature — negative refractive index, perfect absorption, and topological photonics. AI-driven inverse design of metasurfaces for flat optics and cloaking devices.
speaker: Prof. John Joannopoulos

title: Self-Healing Polymers and Adaptive Soft Materials
description: Designing materials that autonomously repair damage through dynamic covalent chemistry and supramolecular interactions. Stretchable electronics, self-healing hydrogels for biomedical applications, and ML for designing dynamic bond networks.
speaker: Prof. Zhenan Bao
